data.name: Dark Scavenger
data.detailed_description:
Dark Scavenger is a bizarre point-and-click RPG adventure with a focus on exploration, gaining loot, and meaningful choices.

Filling the role of a powerful space traveler, you find yourself stranded on a mysterious planet in the company of three eccentric, yet resourceful aliens. As you desperately seek a way to repair your ship, a massive conflict unfolds around you involving warring factions and a sinister force that threatens to destroy them all.

Will you adopt the problems of this world as your own or will you just save yourself?

Key Features

  • Unique Dark Comedy Sci-Fi Narrative driven entirely by your choices. Each encounter has multiple outcomes!

  • Earn Tons of Loot and convert it into bizarre equipment!

  • Deep Turn Based Combat which utilizes equipment combinations to exploit enemy weaknesses!

  • Epic Boss Battles with multiple forms.

  • New Game Plus Mode lets you see what you missed the first time around!

  • Tons of Secrets that you will probably never find.

  • Trading Cards!

reviews.review:
A handful of games out there are just bonkers mad. Straiumium immortaly, or Jazz Punk, or Psychonauts, or this.
Dark Scavenger takes some of the improbable silliness of Superhero League of Hoboken but sets it into a different primitive dump in a remote corner of a backwater galaxy that civilization forgot and RimWorld wouldn't touch.
Tribals, pro-wrestlers, gigantic Spider-Bees, rogue toasters that toast toes, slavers and drunks roam what's left of the world, though in defense of the vinos, water isn't safe to drink. Or swim in. Touching is probably ok, but use a stick or a rusty sword.
Actually, i'm not sure Dark Scavenger is all [i]that[/i] different. Less radioactive sheep, more xenomorph really into mime. That's about it.

It teaches not to pet a tornado, which makes it a winner in my book.


Gameplay is less about deck building and combat or squad management. There is no travelling on a map littered with random encounters. Instead, you move from location to location and select peculiar or threatening things to interact with, and probably poison yourself.

Along the way, you will find or be rewarded with all manner of improbable items. Some are important quest items that can unlock progress or affect encounters but the ordinary stuff can be turned into a new Weapon, a new Tool or a new Ally. Or Servant.
Show an item to your three ... companions. Each one happens to be a ... crafter, let's say and will offer to use the item's properties to create or summon something else.

Weapons, tools and allies/slaves, bonded animals, metagalactic ooze each have a limited number of uses. Most can be used outside combat as well. The rusty sword probably has more uses outside combat. It barely even HAS uses in combat. Rusting further seems to be what it does best.


The writing isn't merely punny, it is good.
It came from a mad brain.
Gameplay is simple but that's just as well. Adding more of the unneccessary would only make it tedious. As it is, Dark Scavenger is a hillarious misadventurous adventure that plays like a breeze and makes enough sense to be enjoyable while not taking itself seriously at all.

Some game designers try to exploit the "surreal" or "nonsensical" theme but try way too hard or play the same few notes over and over again. On rare occasion, someone comes along and just "gets" it. Makes it look easy.
That's the gist of Dark Scavenger.

You could bore yourself with some ordinary game, or you could stray off the beaten path and play something inspired. Embrace making poor life choices like a champion.
